Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our MAP, attached is a concise performance qualification plan we propose to run during the two-week ACME pilot window. High-level items we want to validate in the MAP and sign off on before production rollout:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) targets at cold and warm start
- P95 and P99 latency for 512-token and 2k-token contexts
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency levels (10/50/200 concurrent requests)
- End-to-end cost estimate per 1M tokens under proposed batching/quantization settings

What’s included in the attachment (redwood_bench_plan_v1.pdf): workload definition, test harness instructions (Replay + synthetic spike), success criteria, test schedule, and a barebones reporting template.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You confirm the workload bindings (sample user prompt classes) and any sensitive inputs to exclude.
2) We lock the target SLOs below (suggested in the attached).
3) We run the baseline and optimized passes (3 business days each) and share results + annotated MAP updates.

Suggested pilot timeline: baseline run starts Mon Jul 27, optimized run Aug 1–3, MAP sign-off Aug 5. If procurement needs DocuSign earlier, please loop them in.

Attachments: redwood_bench_plan_v1.pdf (7 pages)

Thanks,

Sergio / Marissa / Laura —

Quick tech scoping answers and proposed success criteria:

Test harness and workload
- We'll ingest ACME's 48h anonymized traces into the replay harness.
- Add a synthetic "agent latency" overlay to simulate remote tool calls (configurable 50–500ms per call).
- Concurrency: we will run sweeps at 10, 50, 100, and 200 concurrent sessions. For 200 concurrency we will use optimized batching + reduced KV storage to keep memory footprint acceptable.

Success criteria (proposed final SLOs to put in the MAP)
- TTFT (warm): p90 < 250ms, p95 < 320ms. Cold TTFT (first request after idle): p90 < 600ms.
- Latency: p95 (512 tokens) < 480ms; p95 (2k tokens) < 1.1s.
- Throughput: sustained 35k tokens/sec aggregate at 100 concurrency (baseline); optimized run target 60k tokens/sec.
- Stability: <1% tail error rate during 1-hour sustained spike at 200 concurrency.

Data handling
- KV cache traces: ephemeral only, retained for 7 days for debugging, deleted thereafter. We can turn off persistence entirely for the pilot if ACME prefers — note that will reduce our ability to profile warm-path behavior.

Deliverables and timing
- Baseline runs: Jul 27–29 (3 days), optimized runs: Aug 2–4 (3 days), result deck + MAP updates: Aug 5.
- We will produce a runbook with exact commands and a short script to replay ACME traces.

I will update the attached bench plan with these SLOs and the 200-concurrency procedures.

—Karthik
